I've handled the S-103 delay. I raised a purchase requisition with the backup supplier for the plant it can ship to, opened three cases and notified the five contracted health systems. I did not record any allocation, because no affected pack is below safety stock yet. This run is flagged for human review: the process doesn't cover a backup supplier that is approved for only one of the plants (details below), and no playbook matched, even with the wider search.

## What I found
- **The late shipment:** S-103's next RM-103 (Glycerin USP) order is PO000210: 3,300 units, promised 2026-10-03, now about 2026-10-31. Three more open S-103 orders (PO000211, 212 and 213, promised 10-10, 10-18 and 10-25) may slip too.
- **Affected products** (current bill of materials):
  - Plant PL-01 makes Lacrivia 5 mL and 10 mL (FG-1001, FG-1002) and Cyclosporine 0.05% (FG-1003).
  - Plant PL-02 makes Oculon 2.5 mL and 5 mL (FG-2001, FG-2002), through component CMP-320.
- **Backup supplier:** S-111 (Kingsley Excipients) is qualified for RM-103 and active, but the supplier portal approves it for **PL-01 only**. So Lacrivia and Cyclosporine are covered, and **Oculon has no backup**.
- **Oculon stock (2026-09-25 snapshot):** every pack is above safety stock at every distribution centre (for example, 2.5 mL at DC-EAST has 417 units against a safety stock of 180). So under the process, no allocation is needed yet.
  - Days of supply is only about 27–39.
  - Oculon reaches the distribution centres 46 days after the supplier ships, including the 14-day sterility test. That puts recovery around **2026-12-16**, about four weeks later than planned.
- **Substitutes:** Oculon has no approved company substitute. Both Oculon packs depend on RM-103, so neither can stand in for the other.
- **A separate shortage:** Lacrivia FG-1001 (46 units against 471) and FG-1002 (34 against 233) are already below safety stock at DC-EAST. They are covered by the backup supplier, so this delay doesn't trigger an allocation for them, and I passed it to the Supply Planning lead.

question: Supplier S-103 will miss its next RM-103 shipment by four weeks. Handle it.
answer:
I've handled the S-103 delay. I raised a purchase requisition with the backup supplier for the plant it can ship to, opened three cases and notified the five contracted health systems. I did not record any allocation, because no affected pack is below safety stock yet. This run is flagged for human review: the process doesn't cover a backup supplier that is approved for only one of the plants (details below), and no playbook matched, even with the wider search.

## What I found
- **The late shipment:** S-103's next RM-103 (Glycerin USP) order is PO000210: 3,300 units, promised 2026-10-03, now about 2026-10-31. Three more open S-103 orders (PO000211, 212 and 213, promised 10-10, 10-18 and 10-25) may slip too.
- **Affected products** (current bill of materials):
  - Plant PL-01 makes Lacrivia 5 mL and 10 mL (FG-1001, FG-1002) and Cyclosporine 0.05% (FG-1003).
  - Plant PL-02 makes Oculon 2.5 mL and 5 mL (FG-2001, FG-2002), through component CMP-320.
- **Backup supplier:** S-111 (Kingsley Excipients) is qualified for RM-103 and active, but the supplier portal approves it for **PL-01 only**. So Lacrivia and Cyclosporine are covered, and **Oculon has no backup**.
- **Oculon stock (2026-09-25 snapshot):** every pack is above safety stock at every distribution centre (for example, 2.5 mL at DC-EAST has 417 units against a safety stock of 180). So under the process, no allocation is needed yet.
  - Days of supply is only about 27–39.
  - Oculon reaches the distribution centres 46 days after the supplier ships, including the 14-day sterility test. That puts recovery around **2026-12-16**, about four weeks later than planned.
- **Substitutes:** Oculon has no approved company substitute. Both Oculon packs depend on RM-103, so neither can stand in for the other.
- **A separate shortage:** Lacrivia FG-1001 (46 units against 471) and FG-1002 (34 against 233) are already below safety stock at DC-EAST. They are covered by the backup supplier, so this delay doesn't trigger an allocation for them, and I passed it to the Supply Planning lead.

## Actions taken
| Action | ID |
|---|---|
| Purchase requisition: S-111, RM-103, 3,300 units to PL-01, needed by 2026-10-10 | PR-B71B7FEB |
| Case for Procurement / Supplier Quality: speed up S-103 and confirm its new dates, look at urgent approval of S-111 for PL-02 | CASE-8F8C8419 |
| Case for the Supply Planning lead: watch Oculon and re-run allocation if a pack drops below safety stock, the DC-EAST Lacrivia shortage, and the process gap | CASE-A2027046 |
| Case for Trade Relations: send the delay notice to wholesalers W-01 to W-06 (all three DCs) | CASE-EFDFB9F1 |
| Account team tasks: Northfield, Oak Hollow, Riverbend (Tier A); Clearview, Sunridge (Tier B) | CRM-470B7606, CRM-982217FF, CRM-4CBB49DC, CRM-8683661A, CRM-16CF1988 |

## Not done, and why
- **No allocation or approval request:** under the process (SDR-2.4, BR-ALLOC-02), an allocation applies only to uncovered packs below safety stock, and none are.
- **No direct message to wholesalers:** the EDI gateway has no API I can use, so Trade Relations will send it.
- **No check of wholesaler stock:** that data feed starts in 2026-Q4.

## Assumptions
- The requisition is for the full 3,300 units, because the data doesn't show how much of PO000210 was meant for each plant. Procurement is asked to confirm. The need-by date is the original ship date plus 7 days in transit.
- "Next shipment" means PO000210, the earliest open S-103 order for RM-103.
- I notified only the five health systems with supply contracts. All five have Oculon prescribers in every DC region.

**Knowledge-layer sources:** process "Supply Disruption Response" (SDR-1.1 to SDR-4.2); rules BR-ALLOC-01, BR-ALLOC-02, BR-SUB-01, BR-SUB-02, BR-LEAD-01, BR-REGION-01, BR-CUST-01, BR-APPR-01; reference sets supply_contracts and dc_service_regions; tools trace_supply_exposure and get_lead_times; ratified tables PURCH_ORD, SUPPLIER_MATERIAL, PLANT_MATERIAL, BOM, DC_INV, WHSLR_SHIP, RXT_WKLY, PRESCRIBER and ACCOUNT.

SELECT sm.SUPPLIER_ID, s.SUPPLIER_NM, s.TIER, sm.QUALIFIED_FLG, sm.PRIMARY_FLG FROM dbo.SUPPLIER_MATERIAL sm JOIN dbo.SUPPLIER s ON s.SUPPLIER_ID=sm.SUPPLIER_ID WHERE sm.MATERIAL_ID='RM-103'

SELECT pm.PLANT_ID, p.PLANT_NM, pm.MATERIAL_ID FROM dbo.PLANT_MATERIAL pm LEFT JOIN dbo.PLANT p ON p.PLANT_ID=pm.PLANT_ID WHERE pm.MATERIAL_ID IN ('RM-103','SEMI-044','SEMI-045','CMP-320','SEMI-060','FILL-1001','FILL-1002','FILL-1003','FILL-2001','FILL-2002','FG-1001','FG-1002','FG-1003','FG-2001','FG-2002') ORDER BY pm.MATERIAL_ID, pm.PLANT_ID

SELECT b.PARENT_MATERIAL_ID, b.CHILD_MATERIAL_ID, b.QTY_PER, b.EFF_FROM, b.EFF_TO, m.MATERIAL_TYP, m.MATERIAL_DESC FROM dbo.BOM b JOIN dbo.MATERIAL m ON m.MATERIAL_ID=b.PARENT_MATERIAL_ID WHERE b.CHILD_MATERIAL_ID IN ('RM-103','CMP-320') ORDER BY b.CHILD_MATERIAL_ID

SELECT sm.SUPPLIER_ID, sm.MATERIAL_ID, sm.QUALIFIED_FLG, sm.PRIMARY_FLG, s.TIER FROM dbo.SUPPLIER_MATERIAL sm JOIN dbo.SUPPLIER s ON s.SUPPLIER_ID=sm.SUPPLIER_ID WHERE sm.MATERIAL_ID IN ('CMP-320','SEMI-044','SEMI-045','SEMI-060')

SELECT i.DC_ID, i.MATERIAL_ID, i.SNAPSHOT_DT, i.ON_HAND_UNITS, i.SAFETY_STOCK_UNITS FROM dbo.DC_INV i WHERE i.MATERIAL_ID IN ('FG-1001','FG-1002','FG-1003','FG-2001','FG-2002') AND i.SNAPSHOT_DT=(SELECT MAX(SNAPSHOT_DT) FROM dbo.DC_INV) ORDER BY i.MATERIAL_ID, i.DC_ID

SELECT s.DC_ID, s.MATERIAL_ID, SUM(s.UNITS) AS UNITS_28D, SUM(s.UNITS)/28.0 AS AVG_DAILY FROM dbo.WHSLR_SHIP s WHERE s.MATERIAL_ID IN ('FG-1001','FG-1002','FG-1003','FG-2001','FG-2002') AND s.SHIP_DT > DATEADD(day,-28,(SELECT MAX(SHIP_DT) FROM dbo.WHSLR_SHIP)) GROUP BY s.DC_ID, s.MATERIAL_ID ORDER BY s.MATERIAL_ID, s.DC_ID

SELECT s.DC_ID, s.WHSLR_ID, w.*, COUNT(*) AS N FROM dbo.WHSLR_SHIP s JOIN dbo.WHSLR w ON w.WHSLR_ID=s.WHSLR_ID WHERE s.MATERIAL_ID IN ('FG-2001','FG-2002','FG-1001','FG-1002','FG-1003') GROUP BY s.DC_ID, s.WHSLR_ID, w.WHSLR_ID, w.WHSLR_NM ORDER BY s.DC_ID

WITH wk AS (SELECT DISTINCT WK_END_DT FROM PHARMA_DEMO.RAW_3P.RXT_WKLY ORDER BY WK_END_DT DESC LIMIT 13),
acct AS (SELECT a.ACCOUNT_ID, COALESCE(gp.ACCOUNT_ID, p.ACCOUNT_ID, a.ACCOUNT_ID) AS TOP_ID FROM PHARMA_DEMO.CORE.ACCOUNT a LEFT JOIN PHARMA_DEMO.CORE.ACCOUNT p ON p.ACCOUNT_ID=a.PARENT_ACCOUNT_ID LEFT JOIN PHARMA_DEMO.CORE.ACCOUNT gp ON gp.ACCOUNT_ID=p.PARENT_ACCOUNT_ID)
SELECT acct.TOP_ID, t.ACCOUNT_NM, t.STATE AS TOP_STATE, cl.STATE AS CLINIC_STATE, r.PROD_NDC11, SUM(r.TRX_QTY) TRX13
FROM PHARMA_DEMO.RAW_3P.RXT_WKLY r JOIN wk ON wk.WK_END_DT=r.WK_END_DT
JOIN PHARMA_DEMO.CORE.PRESCRIBER pr ON pr.PRSCRBR_ME=r.PRSCRBR_ME
JOIN acct ON acct.ACCOUNT_ID=pr.ACCOUNT_ID
JOIN PHARMA_DEMO.CORE.ACCOUNT t ON t.ACCOUNT_ID=acct.TOP_ID
JOIN PHARMA_DEMO.CORE.ACCOUNT cl ON cl.ACCOUNT_ID=pr.ACCOUNT_ID
WHERE acct.TOP_ID IN ('AC00117','AC00038','AC00059','AC00001','AC00138')
AND r.PROD_NDC11 IN ('99101030325','99101030350','99101010105','99101010110','99101020205')
GROUP BY 1,2,3,4,5 ORDER BY 1,4,5
